The Peace of Lodi happened before the Pa.why: True: the Peace of Lodi was signed in 1454, the Pazzi conspiracy struck in 1478 and the Bonfire of the Vanities burned in 1497. Each event is named often, but the three are rarely written together, so the end-to-end order is not a stored sentence that could compete with the edited property.

sources.quote: The Treaty of Lodi, or Peace of Lodi, was a peace agreement which brought to an end the Wars in Lombardy between the Venetian Republic and the Duchy of Milan, signed in the city of Lodi on 9 April 1454.
The attack took place on the morning of Sunday, 26 April 1478, during High Mass at the Duomo of Florence.

The phrase itself usually refers to the bonfire of 7 February 1497, when supporters of the Dominican friar Girolamo Savonarola collected and burned thousands of objects such as cosmetics, art, and books in the public square of Florence, Italy, on the occasion of Shrove Tuesday, martedì grasso.

notes: RBox revision of the topic's transitive relation: 'happened before' becomes intransitive (axiom ¬Trans). The edit is stated positively so the negation and compound questions carry no double negative (the 'not transitive' wording made 3 of 4 models miss the old 'Is it false that ... is not transitive?' wording; the negation is now worded 'Is it true that ... is not intransitive?'). Both readings of 'intransitive' give the same answers, since every instance asks whether the conclusion follows from the two stated links. Instances are less famous events whose dates are rarely recalled together: the Peace of Lodi (1454), the Pazzi conspiracy (1478) and the Bonfire of the Vanities (1497) in Florence, and the battles of Brunanburh (937), Maldon (991) and Assandun (1016). Caveat: a model can still work out the order from dates it holds. Cross-lingual queries ask the first instance; the zh prompt puts the bonfire in quotation marks, since 虚荣之火 is not a settled name. Direct, instance and cross-lingual answers are all 'no' after the edit. Near unrelated asks transitivity of another relation (a leak turns its yes to no); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance facts in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1).
